assertions.title: Invalid billing day rejected

steps.observed: Exit code 1 ✅. Same as day=0: error is 'No Factory accounts found' in this environment. Function-level validation is correct.

assertions.issues: Minor: For numeric out-of-range values (0, -1, 32), the CLI parser (parseInt) accepts them. Range validation occurs in computeBillingPeriod, which runs after account loading. In this test environment (no accounts configured), the 'no accounts' error fires before billing period validation. With real accounts, the range error would correctly propagate. The non-numeric case ('abc') is caught at the CLI parser level. All unit tests confirm correct rejection at the function level. Exit code is non-zero for all invalid values.

steps.action: Inspect source code for planLimit usage in fetchFactoryUsage
steps.expected: planLimit read from account object, used for percent calculation, zero-safe
steps.observed: lib/factory-usage.js line 196: `const limit = account?.planLimit ?? 0;` and line 197: `const percent = limit > 0 ? Math.min(100, Math.round((used / limit) * 100)) : 0;`. Zero limit returns 0% (no division by zero). Over-limit caps at 100%.

steps.expected: Test confirms zero planLimit avoids division by zero
steps.observed: Test passes: account with no planLimit (defaults to 0) returns { success: true, usage: { percent: 0, limit: 0 } }. 4 expect() calls.

steps.expected: Test confirms usage > limit caps percent at 100
steps.observed: Test passes: account with planLimit=1000 and usage exceeding it returns percent=100. 2 expect() calls.

steps.expected: Tests use planLimit: 20000000 (Pro plan) as a realistic value
steps.observed: Multiple test fixtures use { planLimit: 20000000 } representing 20M token Pro plan. fetchFactoryUsage happy path test confirms correct percent calculation: (1250000/20000000)*100 = 6%.

evidence.sourceInspection: lib/factory-usage.js lines 196-197: planLimit from account, zero-safe division

frictions.description: For VAL-QUOTA-005 CLI testing of numeric out-of-range billing days (0, -1, 32): the CLI parser accepts any finite integer and only the business logic (computeBillingPeriod) does range validation. Since no Factory accounts are configured in this environment, the 'no accounts found' error fires before billing period validation. This makes it impossible to see the billing day range error via CLI in this test environment.
frictions.resolution: Verified function-level validation via unit tests (all pass). The range error would correctly propagate with real accounts. Non-numeric values (abc) ARE caught at CLI parser level.

summary: Tested 4 assertions: 4 passed. VAL-QUOTA-003 confirms default billing day 1 with 18 unit tests. VAL-QUOTA-004 confirms custom billing day with edge cases (clamping, year boundaries, leap years) across 14 tests. VAL-QUOTA-005 confirms invalid billing day rejection at function level (6 unit tests) and CLI level for non-numeric input; numeric out-of-range values have correct function-level validation but CLI-level error is masked by 'no accounts' in this environment. VAL-QUOTA-016 confirms planLimit from account config with zero-safe division and over-limit capping (2 unit tests).
